why_not_the_literal_tip.finding: trust origin/main is --locked-UNBUILDABLE at the merge 28220d5879 and at the docs tip dc99dbf67e above it. The merge resolved first-party/ay to f289e7c8 (ay 0.10.0, the ddb545d35b side) and Cargo.lock to the 0.10.0 side, while keeping first-party/trust-mc at 9aa35ad10 (the acb08e7616 side), whose manifest requires ay-encode 0.13.0 from ay.git. No checkout of the ay submodule satisfies both: with ay at f289e7c8 the [patch] ay-encode 0.10.0 cannot satisfy the 0.13.0 requirement (cargo: 'patch was not used in the crate graph'); with ay at 5bd74669 (0.13.0) the committed lock's 0.10.0 path entries mismatch. Either way `cargo metadata --locked` demands a lock update and --locked refuses. Verified both directions this lane.

why_not_the_literal_tip.consequence: the measured driver is acb08e7616 — the newest --locked-buildable commit containing all three emission waves (37f5b4e824 EM, a75907ef0d FR, d2da911e03 WB are all ancestors). The flip-path blobs at acb08e7616 are byte-identical to 28220d5879's (verified file-by-file, both build logs print them); the only compiled-tree delta to the broken tip is compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/clean_origin_mir.rs (+lib.rs comment) — the Clean-origin ANALYSIS-phase arm (f28d6e883e), a path the whole-crate differential of ordinary Rust bodies does not take. At the census-time tip the first-party/ay pin moved again (cc6389c931, lock ay-encode 0.11.0) — buildability there was not measured. The literal-tip number is therefore UNKNOWN, not rounded up; the producer identity for THIS measurement is byte-pinned above, and crates/trust-thir-lower carries zero commits between the measured rev and the census-time tip.
